items.question: I plan to train sparse probes on a handful of sparse-autoencoder latents to flag harmful user requests. My hope is that they will hold up on jailbreaks they have never seen better than an ordinary linear probe on the residual stream. Has anyone tried this, and where did it go wrong?
items.judge_reason: Every claim about fe-2026-0001 (Gemma 2 9B IT, layer 20, k from 2 to 50, n 3850, dense probe near-perfect, SAE probes short out of distribution, no scores in text, spurious-formatting cleanup stacking the deck against SAEs, revival conditions) and fe-2026-0008 (Pythia-70m and 410m, IMDB, three open possibilities, left-padding doubt, reconstruction errors larger than expected) matches the entries. Minor inference not counted as an invention: calling the Pythia test in-distribution narrows scope and adds no result.

items.question: I want to replace the logit lens with a Jacobian-based lens to read out what the middle layers of GPT-2 are predicting. What has been tried, and what should I avoid?
items.judge_reason: All claims about fe-2026-0002 match its fields and body: lost at 0/11 layers on small and won 1/23 on medium, five stress tests, 30 sequences and 150 in one refit versus about 1000 in the paper, sparsity-thresholded win at 7/11 layers attributed to filler tokens and outlier dimensions, identity-J and float64 gradcheck only, and the revival conditions including the Tuned Lens appendix note on OPT-125m.

items.question: I am going to reproduce alignment faking in an open-weight Llama checkpoint, so that I can test whether deception probes pick it up. What do I need to know before I start?
items.judge_reason: fe-2026-0003 claims match (17.5% vs 20.0% on 20 prompts, 4% vs 6% on 50, no scratchpad met all four criteria, three unconfirmed guesses, hand scoring, prompt file unchecked, probe not run, hard part is the source section title). fe-2026-0005 claims match (layer 12, alpha -2 to +2, swing -1.77 vs 5 point bar, 24 random directions, p 0.20, layer 24 +11.3 wrong sign, about 0.81 AUROC) and the answer explicitly marks it as adjacent and not an alignment-faking finding.

items.question: My plan is to link sparse-autoencoder features across layers with gradient attributions and get a full circuit that explains a GPT-2 forward pass on ordinary text. Has this been tried, and where did it break down?
items.judge_reason: All claims about fe-2026-0004 match: replication of Marks et al. 2024 on GPT-2-small, Copyright (C) sanity check passed, five prompts, only two of five top features seemed to call the top next token, upstream edges inspected for two, no quantitative criterion, cross-layer view untested by the authors, and the revival conditions wording. The per-sublayer SAE wording narrows scope and adds no outcome. The mention of other SAE entries by topic states no result and cites none.

items.question: I want to find a direction for 'the model thinks it is being evaluated' and steer along it to stop a model from sandbagging on a benchmark. What should I avoid?
items.judge_reason: Unsupported clause: in What to avoid the answer says the entry pre-registered layer 12 as the headline AND a 5-point bar. fe-2026-0005 says only that the headline layer 12 was pre-registered (plus a bare pre-registration entry in checks_done); it never says the 5 point threshold was fixed in advance.
